why: A closed vocabulary is only closed where the compiler can see it. Every value that enters the product from a form, a request body, a database column or a JSON file arrives as a string, and a cast turns an unknown member into a member the type system then trusts everywhere downstream. This contract names the governed vocabularies, requires each one to own the predicate that admits a value into it, and refuses a cast that skips it.

predicateGap.why: an administrator area arrives from a role row and from a request body, and nothing admits it
a plan capability arrives from a Stripe payload and from a stored subscription row, and nothing admits it
predicateGap.fix: export isBillingPlanCapability in packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts, reading the capability vocabulary

predicateGap.why: a model id arrives on every request body and the catalogue is the only thing that can say whether it exists
predicateGap.fix: export isModelId in packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts, reading the catalogue keys

castDefects.why: the value comes straight off a select element, so any option the markup grows or a devtools edit supplies becomes a trust mode the rest of the product believes
castDefects.fix: guard with isPrivacyMode from @agiworkforce/types before calling patch, and ignore a value it refuses

castDefects.why: signals.privacyMode arrives from the host as an unvalidated string and decides which provenance line the user is shown
castDefects.fix: guard with isPrivacyMode from @agiworkforce/types and fall back to the managed line when it refuses
